title: 2.2.8 Algorithm in Plain English (Part A)
description: Define algorithm in your own words, then write a precise numbered algorithm for an everyday task. AI-graded.
sourceRef: book 2.2.1 — Example 2.1 'A Morning Algorithm', Try It Now 2.1; artifact per curriculum-plan.md A2.2.1 Part A

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Algorithm in Plain English — AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
Part 1 — In your own words, what is an algorithm? (1–2 sentences.)

Part 2 — Write a precise, step-by-step algorithm in plain English (not code) for an everyday task you know well — making a sandwich, tying your shoes, logging into a website, etc. Number the steps. Someone who has never done the task should be able to follow your steps exactly and succeed. Be precise: don't skip steps or assume the reader 'just knows' something.

rubric.title: Defines algorithm in own words
rubric.description: Defines an algorithm as a precise, ordered set of steps to accomplish a task, in the student's own words.

rubric.title: Part 2 uses numbered, ordered steps
rubric.description: Part 2 is a numbered/ordered list of steps in a sensible sequence.

rubric.title: Steps are precise and unambiguous
rubric.description: Steps are precise and unambiguous — no major skipped step or 'and then it's done' hand-wave a beginner couldn't follow.

rubric.title: Steps complete the task from start to finish
rubric.description: The steps, followed exactly, actually accomplish the chosen task from start to finish.
